title: YOCO one-cache with layer-specific reads
hypothesis: A single global cache plus a shared rank-2 basis of layer-specific K/V read transforms can recover aligned cross-layer attention functions with <=75% complete bytes; private residual rank will determine when shared cache reads cease to recover layer-specific functions economically.
physical_object: one global FP32 memory cache C shared by four cross-decoder layers
mirror_coordinate: per-layer coefficients over a shared basis of K/V read transforms plus optional private residual rank q
logical_multiplicity: four layer-specific logical memory functions over one physical cache
controls: independent full K/V layer maps and materialized outputs
native shared-basis/PCA layer coefficients (exact function control)

development.selection_metric: per-layer attention-output NRMSE, complete serialized model/cache bytes, and read-transform MAC proxy across fixed rho/rank grid

paid_objects: independent layer K/V transforms and materialized caches

success_gate: For rho=0 and rho=.1, at least one q<=1 point across all audit seeds has per-layer output NRMSE <=.02, complete payload <=75% independent, and read-transform MAC proxy <=2x independent. Mirror attribution also requires an advantage over native shared-basis/PCA.
failure_gate: No q<=1 point meets quality/bytes/compute at rho=.1, or exact recovery requires payload >= independent. Exact native-basis alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value regardless of generic shared-cache feasibility.
boundaries: Synthetic FP32 cross-layer attention operator screen only; no trained YOCO model, language NLL, GPU kernel, or production throughput claim.
One global cache is held fixed; only layer read maps vary.
Fresh seeds and grid frozen before execution; no audit tuning.
